Head of Product (Remote)

Lightning Labs · Product · Full-time · Remote (US time zones) · Reports to the CEO

 
 

About Lightning Labs

Lightning Labs builds the open infrastructure that makes bitcoin the native money of the internet. Our software powers a large share of the Lightning Network, from LND, the most widely used Lightning implementation, to the tools that let developers, businesses, and now AI agents send and receive bitcoin and stablecoins instantly, at internet scale.

We're building a team that's passionate about cryptography, bitcoin, decentralization, security, and privacy. The next wave of users on the network won't only be people. They'll increasingly be software agents that discover services, negotiate, and pay on their own. We think bitcoin and Lightning are the right payment rails for that world, and we're building for it now.

The Role

We're looking for a Head of Product who embodies those values and who wants to bring bitcoin and Lightning to the masses, both human and machine. You'll own product vision, strategy, and roadmap across the Lightning Labs portfolio, working directly with the CEO, engineering leads, and our go-to-market team.

This is a player-coach role. You'll lead the product organization: product managers, including a PM who owns our core infrastructure (LND, btcd, btcwallet, and DevOps), plus design and technical content writing. You'll stay hands-on: writing specs, making pricing and launch calls, talking to developers and partners, and building prototypes yourself.

You'll also be AI-native. At Lightning Labs, product work runs through tools like Claude Code and Codex. We use them to explore codebases, draft specs, analyze data, and turn an idea into a working prototype or demo in hours instead of weeks. We expect our Head of Product to work this way by default, and to help the rest of the team do the same.

Our Product Stack

You’ll set product direction across the whole stack. Product Managers on the team own the core infrastructure day to day, so your focus will be payments, assets, and agentic commerce. That starts with Wavelength, our newest product: an open-source, agent-first client and SDK built on Ark that lets any app send and receive standard Lightning payments. It is in public alpha, and taking it to broad mainnet adoption is one of your first priorities. Alongside it are Taproot Assets, our protocol for issuing stablecoins and other assets on bitcoin and Lightning, and L402 together with its reverse proxy Aperture, which let machines and agents pay for APIs over HTTP.

Underneath sit the tools node operators use: Lightning Terminal for node and liquidity management, Loop for moving funds between on-chain and off-chain, and Lightning Node Connect for secure remote access. All of it is built on LND, the leading Lightning implementation, used by exchanges, wallets, and payment processors around the world. This is a leadership role for product, which means deciding what we build next and which new products and markets we enter.

Responsibilities

  • Define and own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap across Lightning Labs' products, and make the hard calls on priorities and tradeoffs between them

  • Lead our agentic commerce and payments strategy, figuring out where bitcoin, Lightning, stablecoins, L402, and Wavelength fit as AI agents start to transact on their own

  • Grow Wavelength and push forward broad mainnet adoption, including onboarding, limits, safety rails, developer experience, and network growth

  • Prototype and demo constantly. Use Claude Code, Codex, and similar tools to build working prototypes, reference integrations, and demos that test ideas with developers before engineering commits to them

  • Drive product launches end to end, working with engineering, design, marketing, and developer relations on positioning, messaging, docs, blog posts, and launch goals

  • Set pricing and business models for our hosted services, working from unit economics, liquidity costs, and the competitive landscape

  • Write clearly and often. Explain technical concepts to internal and external audiences through specs, blog posts, launch announcements, docs, and partner materials

  • Work with engineering leads on scope, sequencing, and release readiness, including planning cycles, launch gates, and issue triage across multiple repositories

  • Make our products as easy for AI agents to use as for human developers, with agent-readable docs, MCP servers, skills, and SDKs as first-class parts of the product

  • Lead and grow a team of product managers, designers, and a technical content writer. Set the bar for quality, coach the team, hire well, and model the AI-native way of working

  • Make sure our design and technical content (docs, guides, blog posts, and launch materials) are as good as the products themselves

Minimum Qualifications

  • 7-10 years of product experience, including leading product for developer platforms, APIs, payments, or infrastructure

  • Experience setting product strategy and roadmaps from conception to launch, and leading cross-functional teams through launches

  • A deep, hands-on understanding of how software is built, with experience across development methodologies and an appreciation of the tradeoffs between approaches

  • Daily, hands-on use of AI coding and agent tools such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor in your product work, including building working prototypes and demos yourself. Please show us something you've built

  • Strong interest in agentic commerce and payments: how AI agents will discover, pay for, and sell services, and what payment infrastructure that requires

  • Experience driving product vision, go-to-market strategy, pricing, and design discussions

  • Experience managing and developing product managers, and ideally designers or writers as well

  • Ability to influence engineers, executives, and external partners without direct authority

  • Demonstrated passion for bitcoin and Lightning, along with an understanding of the technology, community, and ecosystem

  • Excellent written communication skills

  • Willingness to work in US time zones

Preferred Qualifications

  • Undergraduate or advanced degree in a technical field, or equivalent experience

  • Experience building bitcoin or Lightning products or services

  • Familiarity with the protocols and standards emerging around agent payments and machine-to-machine commerce (L402, MCP, and the wider ecosystem of agent payment protocols)

  • Experience with stablecoins or asset issuance protocols and platforms is a plus

  • Knowledge of networking and routing concepts and how they apply to Lightning payments

  • Experience shipping developer-facing SDKs, docs, and developer experience, and knowing what makes a developer platform easy to adopt

  • Knowledge of multiple functional areas such as Engineering, UX/UI, Sales, Developer Relations, Customer Support, Finance, or Marketing

About us:

Luno has spent over a decade making digital assets safe to own. Since 2013, we’ve helped millions of people around the world buy, store and invest in crypto, working with regulators in every market and holding all customer crypto 1:1. That discipline built the licences, banking relationships, custody and compliance machinery that the next era of this market will run on. The financial system is moving on-chain. Stablecoins are the only digital asset class operating at institutional scale today, and while 98% of supply is dollar-pegged, roughly half of global payment flows are not. That gap is the opportunity, and it is largest in exactly the markets Luno has spent twelve years building in.

About the team

You will lead the Engineering team building GTXN, Luno's global settlement business. GTXN focuses on institutional payments: the collections, pay-outs, virtual account and conversion products that let businesses and financial institutions move money in and out of emerging markets through one integration.

You will lead GTXN's engineering pods (Payments and OTC), and sit in the GTXN leadership trio alongside the Group Product Manager and the UX Manager. Lead Engineers and a Portfolio Engineer report to you, and you work closely with shared platform teams such as Exchange, Liquidity, Fiat Platform and Transaction Monitoring. You will report to the VP of Engineering for the Luno Group and be a peer to the other Engineering Managers across the organisation.

GTXN has the ambition to operate like a startup, so this role needs a balance between speed and control: you will build engineering teams and payment systems that move fast and that customers, regulators and partners can trust.

The role in a nutshell

You will be accountable for engineering as a whole in GTXN. You will lead and grow the people who build GTXN's payment products, turn the GTXN strategy into an engineering plan that is realistic and delivered, and make sure the systems that move our customers' money are reliable, operable and controlled.

Your mission will be

  • Lead and grow GTXN engineering: Line manage the Lead Engineers and Portfolio Engineer in GTXN. Own hiring, onboarding, performance, calibration and promotions, and build a bench of leaders who can run the pods without depending on you.
  • Own engineering delivery for GTXN: Make sure GTXN's engineering commitments are realistic and get met. Own capacity across the pods, anticipate delivery risk before it materialises, and manage dependencies on the shared platform teams GTXN relies on.
  • Build payment systems that are reliable, operable and controlled: Set the engineering bar for routing, reconciliation, ledger integrity, failure handling, retries and provider redundancy. Work with the Portfolio Engineer and Architecture to make sound design trade-offs as GTXN scales to new corridors and currencies.
  • Own operational excellence: Hold the standard for Launch Plans and Acceptance Into Service across GTXN. Be accountable for incident response, from triage to post-mortem, including payment provider and banking incidents, and learn from them at a systemic level.
  • Partner in the GTXN leadership trio: Work with the Group Product Manager, the UX Manager and the GTXN business leadership to turn strategy into an engineering plan. Be the single engineering voice for GTXN, including pushing back on feasibility, risk or sequencing when needed.
  • Make every corridor faster than the last: Turn bank and payment provider integrations into repeatable engineering capabilities and playbooks, so each new corridor, currency or customer integration takes less effort than the one before.
  • Shape how GTXN engineering works: Design team structure and ways of working for startup pace, raise engineering quality without slowing the team down, and lead the adoption of AI in how the team builds and operates.

A little about you

  • You are a Senior Engineering Manager or engineering leader who has led multiple teams, including managing tech leads or other managers.
  • You have a strong engineering background, and you are a credible technical partner to senior and staff engineers on system design, architecture and trade-offs.
  • You have payments experience: either you have led engineering teams building payment systems, or you built payment systems as an engineer before moving into management. Ideally this includes bank or payment provider integrations, settlement, reconciliation and ledgers.
  • You understand what it takes to run money movement in production: idempotency, retries, failure and return handling, reconciliation breaks and provider outages, and what each costs when it goes wrong.
  • You have run production systems in a regulated environment, and you can balance speed with the controls, auditability and compliance that payments require.
  • You develop people deliberately: you have grown engineers into leads, handled difficult performance conversations directly, and built teams that hold together through change.
  • You are comfortable with ambiguity and pace. You take unclear problems, create structure and ownership around them, and keep the team moving.
  • You communicate clearly with engineers, product, commercial leaders and executives, and you influence outcomes through credibility and well-reasoned positions.
  • Experience with payments in emerging markets, in Africa or Southeast Asia, or with multi-currency, cross-border or stablecoin settlement is a strong advantage.
  • You use AI as part of how you and your teams work, and can show where it has changed your output, not just your tooling.

Life at Luno:

  • Remote but reachable work policy gives you the freedom to choose between working from home or the office.
  • Plus the option to buy and sell up to 5 days leave
  • Improve body and mind, with excellent private medical insurance
  • Enjoy peace of mind with Luno's comprehensive retirement fund and essential risk benefits.
  • Access to Learnably and our additional learning platforms for your personal and professional development
  • 6 months primary care-giver leave
  • Paw-ternity leave for your furry friend
  • Annual Inspiration Day in addition to your annual leave which increases based on your length of service! 
  • A collaborative, friendly work community, with regular social events and virtual cooking, dancing, drawing and house planting classes hosted by our Lunauts
  • Free lunch and snacks
  • 0 fees up to a certain amount with Luno from the day you start.*

*Offer only available on Luno Instant Buy, not Luno Exchange

OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.

OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

 

About the Opportunity

We are seeking a hands-on Structured Products Trader to manage and develop our structured products trading capabilities across digital assets and tokenized or traditional financial assets. The role combines trading and risk ownership with product design, cross-venue hedging, technology delivery, and workflow automation.
 

What You’ll Be Doing 

  • Manage, price, and hedge structured products portfolios, including dual-currency products, vanilla and exotic options, and other yield or option-based solutions.
  • Monitor portfolio Greeks, PnL, scenario risk, liquidity, margin usage, settlement exposure, and venue-level concentrations; escalate material risks promptly.
  • Optimize pricing and hedging across multiple liquidity sources and trading venues, taking account of order-book depth, transaction costs, account margin, and operational constraints.
  • Translate trading requirements into clear product and technology specifications covering calculation logic, units, trade direction, account mapping, configuration priority, exception handling, and acceptance criteria.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Risk, Operations, Sales, and external counterparties to launch and improve structured products and supporting trading infrastructure.

  • Identify production issues, assess customer and trading impact, provide evidence and interim controls, and coordinate investigation and resolution with relevant teams.
  • Build or improve automation for recurring trading, risk, monitoring, and reporting workflows while maintaining appropriate pre-checks, failure controls, auditability, andhuman oversight.
  • Track market developments and client needs, and proactively propose new products, pricing enhancements, risk controls, and process improvements with clear business value.
  • Maintain operating procedures, controls, and knowledge documentation to support resilient day-to-day and out-of-hours coverage.

What We Look For In You

  • At least three years of relevant experience in derivatives trading, structuring, quantitative trading, or a closely related role at a bank, market maker, hedge fund, proprietary trading firm, or digital-asset institution.
  • Strong understanding of options and structured products, including pricing, Greeks, volatility, barriers, settlement mechanics, and hedging risk.
  • Practical experience managing trading-book risk and making decisions under changing liquidity, market, and operational conditions.

About Matter Labs

Matter Labs invented ZK rollups and built the first one on Ethereum: six years in production, over a billion transactions processed, over four billion dollars in value locked. We want programmable money to become a foundation for the next financial system, with institutions able to shape the services they provide and keep authority as their infrastructure evolves.

Prividium is our platform for institutions to build and operate digital asset businesses, with privacy and under their own rules. Prividium Commander is the control plane for digital asset services: an institution decides who can do what and tracks the resulting activity, on Prividium Ledger or on the chains it already runs. Prividium Ledger is a private blockchain with publicly verifiable execution. Prividium Connect gives institutions private, bridgeless transactions across blockchains.

Prividium Ledger runs in production for a number of institutional customers. Keeping those ledgers reliable, and making the next ten cheaper to operate than the first four, is the work this role is hired for.

Remote and global, few approvals, a CEO you can reach, unrestricted access to the best AI tools and the expectation that you use them, and a hiring bar of hell yes or no.

The role

You join the Production Unit, the three-person team that owns ZKsync OS in production for our customers: detection, incidents, rollouts and the service objectives each customer is measured against. Today the work is mostly reactive: on-call, incidents, rollouts, RCAs. The job is to change that. Every page and every manual step is a candidate for a fix in the server, a better alert or an automation. About 30 percent of your time goes to code now, and that share grows as the reactive load shrinks.

You own the environments you are assigned end to end: whether a change is safe to roll out, how an incident gets restored and explained, and whether the customer's service objectives are being met. Component teams own their code; you read it, find the cause, and land the fix.

What you will do:

  • Run production for institutional customers. Hold the First Responder rotation, coordinate incidents to restoration, and write the RCA the customer's engineers read.

  • Decide what ships. Go/no-go on changes to your environments, verification before rollout and validation after, including executing sequencer rollouts.

  • Remove the cause. Turn pages, runbooks and manual steps into fixes in the sequencer, provers or tooling, so the same incident does not come back.

  • Measure the service. Own the SLA card for your customers, measured monthly against their contracts.

  • Finish across teams. Drive diagnosis and fixes through the component teams that own the code, without waiting to be asked.

  • Later, support customers who run the chain themselves, where the fix has to work in someone else's hands.

Within a year, on-call load in your environments is measurably lower because of what you shipped, and the unit can take on the next customer without adding people.

What we look for

  • You have been on-call for a system you wrote code for, and you have owned an incident from page to RCA to the fix that stopped it recurring.

  • You find causes in code you did not write. Strong in a systems language such as Rust, Go, C++ or Java; Rust is learnable here.

  • You verify before you roll out and you can say which changes are reversible and which are not.

  • You have run production for a service with external customers, and your incident notices and RCAs were read by their engineers.

  • You make other teams finish the work without escalating.

  • You are willing to hold a 24/7 rotation.

Nice to have: rollup or node operations experience (sequencer, prover, L1 settlement); Ethereum execution client internals; tooling you built that other teams adopted.

If you meet most of this and the rest is learnable, apply anyway.

Not this role

This is not a Forward Deployed Engineer role, which builds and deploys for a customer from discovery to production readiness; this role operates what is in production. It is not DevOps (clusters, network, L1 nodes, backups and disaster recovery stay with DevOps), not partner management, and not a people-management role.

Compensation and work model

  • Base salary range: USD 192,000 to 230,000 per year. Where an offer lands in the range depends on demonstrated scope and results against the bar described above. For candidates in the EU the same range applies

  • Performance-based variable compensation and a long-term token incentive are additional.

  • Benefits (employees): medical, dental and vision from day one, global health cover for team members outside the US; 401(k) with a Safe Harbor match up to 4 percent for eligible US employees, flexible paid time off plus public holidays and two company closure weeks a year; six weeks paid parental bonding leave plus up to ten weeks paid birth recovery leave; confidential mental health support; a USD 2,000 home office stipend, a company laptop refreshed every three years, up to USD 400 a month toward coworking, and a USD 500 annual learning budget; company and team offsites.

  • Fully remote. You must be based in the US or the EU, with the US preferred; some of our customers whitelist the jurisdictions their operators work from, so this is a hard requirement.

  • Full-time, as an employee or a contractor.

  • 24/7 First Responder rotation shared with the Production Unit. Everyone in this role is on it.

  • We do not ask about your current or past pay at any stage of the process.
